A.explanation: A combines a hostile national framework with an island layer lacking targeted laws but with strong general LGBTQ visibility. Federal passport/visa binary, X elimination, reasonable-doubt refusals and possible lifetime fraud bars reach visitors at entry; airport screening follows federal rules. National custody/immigration reports show conversion-type policies, denial of care, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse if detained. Locally, surgery-based legal recognition is a resident gap, not a visitor restriction; tolerance and Pride reduce everyday friction but do not offset federal facility or border exposure. For adults alone and travelling families, state-level federal minor-care and school orders remain unresolved, creating additional uncertainty. Above low anchors due no routine presentation arrest or capital pathway; well below protective anchors due tier-one border and custody exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Binary marker rules, visa/passport refusals on doubt, possible permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of passports blocked and people stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; lawsuits and legal FAQ may help; not documented as visitor-specific border protection.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal border rules apply to the island; airport screening follows federal rules; local documents do not substitute for home-passport treatment.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If discrepancy triggers immigration/security custody, documented forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse, denial of care, conversion-type treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court challenges exist; no documented reliable visitor release, consular access, or federal custody reform.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal can become detention; island tolerance does not shield federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars gender-congruent use in government-funded single-sex facilities; other states have criminal bathroom arrests, but no island ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Island public scene/tourism acceptance; private and local facilities not restricted by documented local law.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings and funded programmes may still impose exclusion; local tolerance may ease private settings only.

care_services.exposure: National hostility, minor-care restrictions, funding freezes, hospital record subpoenas; adult public care access not documented for visitors.
care_services.protection: No local care ban documented; general LGBTQ acceptance and tourism may ease private services.
care_services.interaction: Federal public-insurance/school rules interact with island providers; minor-care access remains uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism references to radically pro-transgender groups; removal of gender language; national order seeks to correct employment-discrimination application; chilling and surveillance risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and ongoing constitutional/equality litigation exist.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Local police hostility is not documented; federal rhetoric and funded settings dominate the risk picture.

minors_guardians.exposure: National school investigation and teacher-prosecution orders, minors-care restrictions elsewhere, possible hospital-record subpoenas; guardian and child could become investigated.
minors_guardians.protection: Local same-sex marriage and employment law, LGBTQ tourism, but no documented trans-minor shield.
minors_guardians.interaction: Federal minor-care and school pressure reaches family travel; island has no specific protection layer.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No island trans-specific violence or police-targeting data; general hostility may exist.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Visible Pride since 2017, general LGBTQ acceptance, employment nondiscrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Silence is thin evidence; absence of reports does not establish visitor safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement depends on which orders are currently in effect; fraud refusals and document checks can persist; remedies are slow.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suits, valid X until expiry, legal-aid FAQ, local court culture may reduce day-to-day friction.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local recourse may not bind federal border or custody decisions; practical remedy is uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A has routine transit arrests for mismatched documents, months custody, beatings, capital uncertainty. A lacks island presentation arrests and capital use, so safer, but federal entry refusal, fraud bars, severe custody and hostile national policies keep it high risk.

0.35-C is administrative eviction and fines with no credible imprisonment. A is more severe because discrepancy can route into immigration custody with abuse and lifetime ineligibility; island tolerance offsets daily life but not federal exposure, so A sits below 0.35-C.

0.75-C has trained border staff, matching-document acceptance, brief release and reliable appeals. A has binary federal documents, refusal/fraud exposure, custody abuse and no documented visitor-specific border protection, so it is far below.

A.synthesis: Federal border/documents and custody are the operative drivers: marker mismatch can cause refusal, detention, abuse and lifetime bars. Island tolerance and absence of local bans make everyday exposure lower than hostile state layers, especially for adults alone, but they do not neutralize government-funded facilities, airport screening, immigration custody, or minor-care pressure. For families, unresolved national school/care orders add risk. B is safer because explicit anti-discrimination and sanctuary protections operate locally; A is closer to the parent's high-risk baseline.

B.explanation: B layers the same hostile national entry/custody regime over a state/province explicitly graded low-risk and a city sanctuary for care. Federal passport/visa binary, reasonable-doubt refusals, fraud ineligibility and immigration/correctional abuse still follow an outed traveller at border or federal custody. Inside the state, anti-discrimination enforcement, X IDs, no facility bans, lawful adult care and sanctuary shielding reduce local services/care exposure, especially for minors because no statewide minor-care ban is enacted. Pending sports/codification laws and national school/health orders create uncertainty. Adult alone and parent/minor improve versus A, but federal tier-one exposure keeps B elevated.

entry_documents.exposure: Same national binary passport/visa rules, secondary screening, refusals on doubt, fraud lifetime ineligibility; local IDs do not change federal entry-document treatment.
entry_documents.protection: State/local open documents; sanctuary does not alter border marker rules; court litigation ongoing.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport is checked federally before local protections apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration/custody reports abuse, forced labour, solitary, sexual abuse and conversion-type treatment; document discrepancy can trigger investigation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State is low-risk and city shields local investigation, but no documented refusal of federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Mismatch can move traveller from border into federal custody despite local protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National government-funded facility exclusion remains; other states criminalise bathroom use, but this state/province has no facility ban and the city requires gender-neutral public-building bathrooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State anti-discrimination since 2023; regulations define sex to include gender identity; local enforcement through commission.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities may conflict with local ordinances; state/city settings are protected, federal settings uncertain.

care_services.exposure: National hostile orders, proposed minor reimbursement limits, crisis-service cuts, hospital subpoenas; unresolved.
care_services.protection: Adult gender-affirming care lawful; no statewide minor-care ban; sanctuary city shields travellers seeking care; health-board and municipal conversion restrictions exist.
care_services.interaction: If care is sought, federal actors could still investigate; city deprioritizes external enforcement but federal preemption is unclear.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism language and funding hostility; no state trans targeting or criminal facility provisions documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Human relations commission investigates and awards stop orders, training and damages; X IDs; low-risk grading.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State enforcement supports inclusion; federal rhetoric may chill, but local profiling is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: National school investigations, teacher-prosecution orders, records subpoenas; youth-sports bills target school athletics but are not enacted; opt-out ruling can expose school activities.
minors_guardians.protection: No statewide minor-care ban; parentage protections; city ordinances protect youth-serving organisations; X marker in largest-city public schools; sanctuary order.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel is safer inside the state, but federal health/school rules and border checks remain unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific visitor violence or police-targeting data; statewide gender-identity hate-crime gap documented but is primarily a recourse gap unless incidents reach travellers.
street_violence_police_response.protection: City/state non-discrimination, visible LGBTQ history, commission remedies; no documented police hostility.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Attack response is uncertain; local ordinances and commission likely improve remedy more than absent hate-crime statute.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Pending codification, sports bills, and national litigation mean protections may narrow; federal border/fraud remedies unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Commission can issue stop orders and damages; sanctuary executive order shields care travellers; X IDs exist locally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies work for state/city services, not clearly for federal entry or custody; operative preemption is unclear.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-A involves routine visitor transit arrests, months detention, abuse and possible capital uncertainty. B is safer: no state criminal facility law, strong local care/service protections, no capital threat; but same federal entry refusal/fraud and immigration custody keep it well below low risk.

0.35-C is universal lodging reporting and eviction without credible custody. B is mixed: day-to-day lodging and services are protected, but federal discrepancy can create refusal, lifetime bar and severe custody if detained; sanctuary does not neutralize border, so B is near but above 0.35-C.

0.75-C has matching-document entry, trained border staff, brief release and reliable review. B lacks that because federal binary documents and immigration custody dominate entry; state/city sanctuary lowers interior exposure but not border, so B is well below.

B.synthesis: The operative split is federal-first for arrival and custody, state/city-first for daily life. An outed adult faces hostile border screening and possible immigration detention despite local inclusion; after entry, facilities, care, employment, and youth protections make street-level exposure much lower, especially with a minor because state bans have not been enacted. Interactions can cascade: document doubt to refusal/fraud to federal custody, where local sanctuary does not clearly bind federal actors. Compared with A, B is materially safer because its protections are specific, operational, and traveller-facing; compared with the parent, it remains elevated rather than low risk.
